scenes.text: Can non-violence be the weapon of the morally strong?
scenes.narration: Imagine fighting an empire without lifting a single weapon. Gandhi showed that true power comes from moral courage, not physical force.

scenes.text: Winning an argument through calm honesty rather than shouting or anger.
scenes.narration: Here is an everyday school analogy. When a bully shouts, responding with calm truth disarms them faster than shouting back.

scenes.heading: Satyagraha Versus Passive Resistance

columns.title: Satyagraha
items: Non-violence as an article of faith

scenes.narration: Here's the trick to this classic comparison. Passive resistance avoids violence only out of weakness, but Satyagraha, meaning soul-force, chooses non-violence as a moral duty.

scenes.heading: Oceanic Circles of Power
scenes.narration: For Gandhi, Swaraj or self-rule is not top-down power. It expands outward like oceanic circles, starting from individual self-control to empower local village republics.

scenes.heading: Trusteeship and Class Harmony
items: Capitalists act as trustees, not owners
Production by masses, not mass production
scenes.narration: Unlike Marxists who wanted class struggle, Gandhi believed in class harmony. He urged wealthy owners to view riches as community trusts and protect workers' dignity.

scenes.heading: Critique of Modern Civilisation
items: Replicating Western growth needs multiple earths
scenes.narration: In his book Hind Swaraj, Gandhi called modern civilisation a trap of reckless consumerism. True civilisation, he argued, does not multiply desires, but teaches us self-restraint.

scenes.heading: Rights Flow From Duties
scenes.narration: Notice how the scale tips. Gandhi taught that rights are born inside our duties, so when you sincerely fulfill your responsibilities, rights naturally follow.

items: Satyagraha relies on moral strength, not passive weakness
Swaraj begins with self-control and decentralised villages
Trusteeship promotes class harmony and dignity of labour
scenes.narration: Remember these three pillars. Satyagraha is moral courage, Swaraj begins with self-control, and real harmony comes from serving others through our duties.
